minutes.headline: Finance Committee took no budget votes; it heard FY20 closeout results and agreed to pilot shared file storage.
minutes.summary: The committee heard public comment and committee reports on COVID effects, parks and the TC Passios building, and asked about building-project evaluation. The finance director reported FY20 revenue and spending closeout results and answered capital-plan and encumbrance questions. Members discussed file-sharing options, and the July 23 minutes were held for later after the motion was withdrawn.

public_comment.topic: Peter noted the passing of longtime resident Bruce Smith.
Statement clarifying the schools' remote learning model, edgenuity-type course cost, registration deadline and switching each quarter.
Jay urged members to watch the Board of Assessors meeting about assessing software problems and possible late tax bills.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no budget votes at this meeting.
The finance director reported FY20 closeout: revenues came in above estimates and spending under budget, so free cash is expected to rise.
The finance director said funds have never been shifted among capital projects, after a member questioned a bylaw allowing administrative moves of capital funds.
The July 23 minutes were held to a later agenda after the motion to approve them was withdrawn.
Chris will keep exploring shared file storage with the town IT contact, and will lead a discussion of a building-project evaluation rubric at the next meeting.

why_it_matters: Higher free cash gives Town Meeting more money to work with when setting the next budget and the tax rate, and the capital-plan questions bear on how closely capital funds are tracked.
A building-project rubric could shape how future building articles are judged before residents are asked to vote on them.
watch_next: Next meeting set for September 10th: minutes, budget discussion after the selectmen's meeting, and the building-project rubric are on the agenda.
